extracted.intended_audience: statesmen, legislators, constitution drafters, political philosophers, and educated public interested in republican constitution-making
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and prescriptive principles for creating and evaluating republican constitutions (stable representative governments) — focused on separation of powers, representation, anti‑corruption devices, and civic institutions. Drawn from John Adams's discussion of what makes American-style constitutions durable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of three orders (three branches)
rubrics_metrics.description: Without three orders, and an effectual balance between them, in every American constitution, frequent unavoidable revolutions are destined to occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adams repeatedly urges a constitution composed of three divisions (a governor/executive, a senate, and a house of representatives). He invokes Cicero and Tacitus to argue that the harmony of distinct orders—arranged skillfully—produces stability and justice; when confused, they produce perpetual faction and violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of executive from legislative power
rubrics_metrics.description: A free people's rights and liberties, and the democratical mixture in a constitution, can never be preserved without a strong executive, i.e., without separating the executive power from the legislative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If executive power (or any considerable part of it) is left in the hands of an aristocratic or democratic assembly, it will corrupt the legislature as rust corrupts iron; when the legislature is corrupted, the people are undone. Thus keep executive functions distinct to protect the legislature and public liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative assembly should mirror the people ('likeness')
rubrics_metrics.description: The end to be aimed at in the formation of a representative assembly seems to be the sense of the people, the public voice: the perfection of the portrait consists in its likeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation may be determined by numbers, property, or both; proportions of electors and members are an affair of calculation. The representative body's composition should be such that it truly reflects the people it governs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term length: keep deputies responsive to constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: The duration [of representatives' terms] should not be so long that the deputy should have time to forget the opinions of his constituents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter terms reduce the disconnect between representatives and the electorate; term design is a lever against corruption and apathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent corruption in elections
rubrics_metrics.description: Corruption in elections is the great enemy of freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt provisions such as more frequent elections and a more general privilege of voting; additionally, structural fixes: dividing districts, diminishing travel distances, and confining the choice to residents to reduce opportunities for bribery and undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a senate to separate elites from the popular house
rubrics_metrics.description: The most illustrious of the people must therefore be separated from the mass and placed by themselves in a senate: this is, to all honest and useful intents, an ostracism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A senate composed of wealthy, noble, and able citizens provides an outlet for ambition and a check on the house of representatives: powerful individuals can be admitted safely to the senate so their influence does not dominate the popular assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checks and balances including negative powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each division should have the power to defend itself by a negative; giving each division a defensive negative makes the system solid and durable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modelled on the English practice, providing mutual negative checks (veto-like privileges) among branches is key to stability. When arranged skillfully the divisions produce harmony; when confused they create destructive conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent judiciary and tribunals to register and apply laws
rubrics_metrics.description: By the erection of various tribunals, to register the laws, and exercise the judicial power — a control has been established over ministers of state and royal councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create tribunals with the authority to interpret and register laws separate from the legislative and executive to restrain abuses and to stabilize government practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to timely public trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving an absolute right to demand a public trial in a certain reasonable time is a important protection for personal liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adams notes that if religious toleration and personal liberty (anchored by the right to a prompt public trial) were more protected, governments would be nearer to being 'governments of laws not of men.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Security of property and personal liberty as constitutional objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Property should be generally secure, and personal liberty seldom invaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutions should aim to secure property rights and protect personal freedoms as central measures of good government and preconditions for commerce and improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for press and public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The press has great influence, even where it is not expressly tolerated; public opinion must be respected by a minister, or his place becomes insecure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept and protect a robust press and public opinion as essential accountability mechanisms: ministers must heed them or suffer loss of office and legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local civic institutions (towns/districts) as foundations of republican virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Towns or districts (local corporations) which confer powers such as repairing roads, choosing officers, assembling to deliberate, and choosing representatives are principal sources where the sentiments of the people are first formed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage municipal corporations and district assemblies that habituate citizens to deliberation, judgement, and participation; these local forums seed public opinion and republican habits vital for the broader state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious societies with locally chosen clergy supportive of liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: Churches are religious societies which include the whole people; clergy are chosen by the people of their parish and have little authority outside their moral example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adams argues that clergy who live among parishioners, are married, and exercise charity cultivate civic virtue; popular selection of clergy ties religious institutions to local republican norms rather than hierarchical power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public primary education in every town
rubrics_metrics.description: There are schools in every town; every town consisting of sixty families is obliged, under penalty, to maintain a school and a master who teaches writing, arithmetic, and the elements of Latin and Greek.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide universal access to elementary schooling to prepare students for colleges and for public life; education is foundational for an informed electorate and capable magistracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal militia enrollment and readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The militia comprises all the people: male inhabitants between 16 and 60 are enrolled and obliged to keep arms and ammunition at their own expense so the country is ready to defend itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A widely-diffused militia fosters civic responsibility and readiness to defend liberties; laws should require enrollment, regular assembly for inspection and drills, and private provision of basic arms and accoutrements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional design of electors and members (districting and franchise rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers, or property, or both, should be the rule; the proportions of electors and members are an affair of calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the franchise and apportionment rules deliberately (by calculation) to achieve desired representation; adjusting who elects and how many representatives per district affects balance, influence, and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concentrating administrative secrecy and spying
rubrics_metrics.description: In a simple monarchy, secrecy in the executive breeds jealousy and the encouragement of informers and spies which poison private life; in a free government ministers are obliged to declare opinions in council, reducing this danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure institutions to minimize a culture of secret intelligence and informers: openness of executive councils and public debate reduces systemic paranoia and abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitution-making as comparative, reasoned, and experimental craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions and committees adopted the method of a wise architect: consult writers, examine celebrated models, compare theories with nature, adopt advantages and reject inconveniences — legislation is an ordinary art and science, not divine revelation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft constitutions by informed comparison of historical models and practical adaptation to circumstances rather than by appeals to miraculous legitimacy; treat political institutions as long-term experiments requiring deliberation and adjustment.
